whenToUse: There are five or more options and people choose several.
It must take little room in a form.
People need to remove chosen items one by one.
whenNotToUse: There are only a few options (lay them out as checkboxes or filter chips).
People need to add values not in the list (use a tag input).
Only one is chosen (use a select).

alternatives.name: Checkbox
alternatives.reason: Few enough options to lay out.

accessibility: The button connects to the list with aria-haspopup="listbox" and aria-expanded, and its name includes the number chosen.
The list is an aria-multiselectable listbox, and each option has aria-selected.
↑/↓ move, Space or Enter chooses, and closing with Esc or Tab returns focus to the button.
Each chip has a remove button with a name such as "Remove development".
